h1: Instagram Story Ad Images Built Around a Square Product Photo
lead: Instagram Story ad images from this template are square product photos for a 9:16 Story canvas. Add the image to the layout in your design tool, then place your headline, price, and offer around it.
intro: This template gives you a square product image with a scene that can sit inside an Instagram or Facebook Story design. Place the image in the middle of a tall canvas, keep the upper and lower areas open for your headline and offer, and finish the layout in Canva or Ads Manager.

A square photo can also be used in feed posts, carousels, and listing galleries, or placed in a Story layout. For full-screen movement, use the [Video Ads tool](/ai-video-generation/ugc-ad-video) and choose a 9:16 video frame.
tip: Keep the product clear in the square image, then reserve the top and bottom of the Story canvas for your account name, headline, price, and ad button.

faq.q: Can the story image include my price or discount code?
faq.a: Put them on after downloading, using Canva, CapCut, or Ads Manager. Words generated inside an image can come out misspelled, so it's made without text.

faq.q: Can I mention SPF or skin benefits in the ad?
faq.a: Stick to the wording printed on your product's label, and add it as text yourself. The image shows the product in its setting and shouldn't promise results like protection or clearer skin.

faq.q: Why not crop a square photo to fit Stories?
faq.a: A square image remains easy to inspect when it sits inside a Story layout with space around it. Place it on a tall canvas and add your headline, price, and code around the image. If you need the product to move across the full phone screen, make a separate 9:16 video instead.

faq.q: What dimensions should an Instagram Story image use?
faq.a: This template outputs a square still, not a finished Story-size file. Place it on a 9:16 canvas in your design tool.

faq.q: How much room should I leave for Story text?
faq.a: Ask for open space across the top or bottom third so your headline fits without covering the product.

faq.q: Can a Story photo be reused for other offers?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the text separate and update the headline or date for different campaigns.

faq.q: What does a Story-ready photo cost?
Can I use the square result in Facebook Stories too?
faq.a: Yes. Place the square image inside a 9:16 Facebook or Instagram Story layout and add the platform text, price, date, and action button yourself. Keep the product away from the header and lower controls, and preview both placements before publishing.

faq.q: What is the safe area for an Instagram Story?
faq.a: Keep the square product and any critical detail inside the center of the 9:16 canvas. Leave the top and bottom zones open for the account header, headline, stickers, and action controls, then check the platform preview.

faq.q: Could a sticker or CTA cover the product?
faq.a: Yes. Place the product away from the top header and lower action area, and preview the finished Story with stickers and the button visible before publishing.

faq.q: Can I reuse the square image in a feed or carousel?
faq.a: Yes. The same square download can run in a feed post, carousel, or listing gallery. Change the surrounding text in your editor while keeping the product and offer details accurate.

visual.overview: A Story ad works when one product remains easy to find while the surrounding canvas leaves room for an exact message. Create a square scene, place it on a 9:16 layout, and finish the offer in your editor for [Instagram ads](/platforms/instagram-ads), [Facebook Stories](/platforms/facebook-ads), or a seasonal [holiday campaign](/occasions/holidays). Keep the product away from the account header and action controls, and use the source label for claims, dates, prices, and codes instead of asking the image generator to typeset them. The square asset is a component of the finished Story, so plan the empty space before you choose a scene.

picker.title: Choose a product scene for a Story ad
picker.lead: Choose a Story scene by the message you need to add later: a product demo, a gift reveal, a creator review, or a simple problem-to-fix moment. Keep one adult action and a quiet area for the headline so the finished frame remains readable on a phone. The prompt examples cover common ad openings, while the uploaded product remains consistent: describe the single action, leave the quiet area visible, and stop on a frame where the label can be read. Add any seasonal wording, discount, or disclaimer only after download. A calm background keeps the product legible behind stickers and buttons, while separate text layers let you change a date or offer without regenerating the image. Keep seasonal wording, discounts, disclaimers, and platform text in separate layers so you can update the offer without regenerating the product scene.
